title: channel.py:77,136: Out-of-bounds channel index when n_channels <= 2
description: The expression n = max(n_channels - 1, 2) followed by return 1 + (h % n) can return channel indices beyond n_channels when n_channels <= 2. For n_channels=1, returns 1 or 2 (valid: 0). For n_channels=2, returns 1 or 2 (valid: 0-1). This violates the function contract and could cause array index out-of-bounds or undefined radio behavior. Same bug in synchronized_hop_channel (line 77) and select_channel hash-based path (line 136). Fix: Add validation if n_channels < 3: return 0 or clamp the result.
close_reason: Fixed: Added edge case handling for n_channels <= 2 in synchronized_hop_channel and select_channel hash-based path. Now returns 0 for n_channels=1 (only control channel exists) and 1 for n_channels=2 (only one data channel). Verified all channel indices stay within [0, n_channels-1] bounds. Tests pass.
